concept.name: Token unlock
concept.definition: A token unlock is the scheduled release of previously locked tokens (team, investor, advisor or ecosystem allocations) into transferable circulation under a project's vesting terms — a predictable supply shock that markets typically front-run.
concept.intuition: It is the day the dam gate opens on insider stock: a known date when a tranche of supply becomes sellable for the first time.
concept.mechanics: Vesting contracts release allocations at cliffs and/or linearly per the published schedule; trackers (e.g. Tokenomist, DefiLlama) index these events. Keyrock's analysis of 16,000+ unlocks found ~90% create negative price pressure, with effects starting ~30 days before the event and team unlocks producing the worst drawdowns (~−25% on average).
concept.failure_modes: Unlocks concentrate sell pressure at known dates, inviting front-running and volatility; opaque or renegotiated schedules destroy predictability, and large unlocks into thin markets can trigger cascading drawdowns.
concept.misconceptions: An unlock is not new inflation — it is previously counted total supply becoming liquid, though the price effect can be identical. Not all unlocks dump equally: ecosystem-development unlocks historically showed slightly positive average effects, while team unlocks were the most negative.
concept.example: A token with $200M market cap unlocking $40M (20% of float) for team and seed investors sees price slide weeks ahead of the date as traders position for the predictable supply expansion.

citations.source: Keyrock research - From Locked to Liquidity: What 16,000+ Token Unlocks Teach Us
